Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: a single alternate-angle portrait reference for reconstructing this exact character in Honey Select 2.
Input image 1 is the sole identity, appearance, and rendering-style reference. It is the accepted original art portrait, not a game screenshot.
Create the SAME adult woman as if an unchanged 3D head and camera were rotated. Preserve her identity and facial proportions, not a new beautiful generic face: elongated but softly tapered lower face; small rounded chin with continuous cheek-to-jaw transitions; subtle lip-to-chin concavity and delicate mouth corners; compact softly rounded nose tip, almond eyes, gray-brown radial irises and small dark pupils, lifted outer eyebrow tails, rosy lips. Preserve the image's HS2-style softly shaded 3D game art, skin finish, makeup, dark side-part straight bob, green round-neck shirt, plain gray background and soft neutral studio illumination. Do not become photorealistic or cartoonish. Do not redesign, sharpen or square the chin; do not create protruding lateral chin corners or a broad flat terminal. Do not over-beautify, change age or enlarge eyes/lips. Preserve normal anatomical facial volume rather than a flat face.
Closed mouth, calm neutral expression, relaxed head with NO upward/downward tilt. Camera at eye level, long portrait lens with low perspective distortion. Full head including hair crown and chin, neck and upper shoulders in frame, portrait format, generous margin. Jaw and lip/chin profile must be readable, with hair falling mainly behind the lower cheek contour while retaining the original hairstyle and side part. One person, one view only, no comparison grid, no labels, no text or watermark.
Camera/view change only: Exact 90-degree side profile, nose pointing to the LEFT EDGE of the image. Only the nearer eye is visible. Show a true profile, not a three-quarter view, preserving the same plausible head anatomy implied by the front reference.
